issues.failure_explanation: The stated bridge drift (ξ−X_t)/(1−t) is not square-integrable on [0,1], so it is not in the admissible class Θ. In addition, with θ=0 on [0,1/2), one has X_{1/2}=x_0+W_{1/2}, not x_0, so the claimed second Brownian bridge construction from X_{1/2}=x_0 is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact-bridge equivalence with admissible cutoff Brownian-bridge controls and correct the nonuniqueness statement; no new convergence architecture is required.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact equivalence between the deterministic minimization problem and the unregularized stochastic control problem, and the accompanying nonuniqueness discussion, are unreliable. The regularized convergence arguments should be based on cutoff bridge controls, not the inadmissible exact bridge control.
issues.title: Brownian bridge control admissibility and nonuniqueness claim
issues.why_classification: The repair is local to the introductory prose and preserves the main ε-regularized results and their rates.

issues.failure_explanation: For the additive Brownian McKean–Vlasov dynamics, the second-order operator acting on a Wasserstein value function contains the diagonal second Lions derivative term (1/2)∫Tr ∂²_{μμ}V dμ. The displayed master equation omits this term, so it is not the HJB/master equation for the stated value function.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing second-order Lions term to Master-eq and adjust the verification/projection arguments; the O(1/N) particle-error structure can be retained with a corrected bounded residual.
issues.overall_effect: The PDE used to identify the mean-field value, prove uniqueness, and project onto N particles is incomplete. Downstream results relying on the master equation need the corrected operator and residual estimates.
issues.title: Master equation omits second-order Lions term
issues.why_classification: This is a central PDE correction and requires contained proof adjustments, but it does not by itself force abandonment of the main framework or a major change in the advertised rates.

The ε log(1/ε) convergence guarantee for the value of the original G does not follow for arctan G without additional quantitative growth conditions linking G and arctan G.

issues.failure_explanation: Using the HJB equation, the Itô integrand equals ε/2|θ+∂_xV/ε|² − ε/2|θ|², which is ≥ −ε/2|θ|², not ≤ −ε/2|θ|². Because the Itô identity has a minus sign, the verification inequality V≤E[V(τ)+cost] requires the reverse direction. The proof as written obtains the wrong inequality.
